Earlier this month, Google released the brand new Pixel 11 series. While the phone itself hasn't changed much compared to its predecessor, the Pixel 10, it has added several thoughtful quality-of-life improvements. One of these is a new camera processing option that gives you more detailed control over how your photos turn out.

With the iPhone 18 Pro just around the corner, I hope Apple will add a similar feature.

The Pixel 11 introduced a new camera feature called Camera Looks. This feature is somewhat similar to "Photographic Styles" on the iPhone, allowing users to adjust how the camera takes photos. These adjustments are made before shooting, and it's not just a simple filter.

Google offers many preset style options similar to Apple's, and you can even fine-tune the effect of each preset. In addition, there are several new options that capture new trends in fluid photography, including Editorial, Velvet, Classic, Digi, Black Tie, and Minimal.

These Looks are deliberately designed to shed the highly computational feel of smartphone photos, trying to recreate the flavor of photos from the old days. As the name suggests, Digi aims to recreate the low dynamic range, high contrast, and grainy look of those small, pocket-sized cameras from the 2010s.

As for Minimal, it takes a completely low-computational approach. Most HDR processes won't run, and you'll basically see what the smartphone's image sensor actually captures. You can see some sample photos at 9to5Google.

Using the iPhone's ProRAW format, theoretically, you can restore an iPhone photo to a state that looks like it hasn't gone through too much post-processing, but doing so somewhat defeats the purpose of using a smartphone to take pictures.

Summary

If Apple wants to build the best pocket camera on the market, it needs to understand that not every user wants the same thing. "Photographic Styles" is a good start, but Apple could go further. Ultimately, photography is an art of self-expression, so giving users more options to control the degree of processing in their photos would be a very important step. Apple should take a cue from Google and add a "Minimal" style to the iPhone.

What do you think of the iPhone's photography performance right now? Do you like Apple's latest "Photographic Styles"? Or do you think it still has shortcomings? I'd love to hear your thoughts; feel free to share them in the comments.
